Construct rolling-origin forecasting folds

Source: R/temporal.R
forecast_folds.Rd

Assessment observations are strictly after the origin and gap and no later than the horizon endpoint. Every future observation, including observations beyond the horizon, is omitted. Sliding windows also omit old observations. Other independent domains remain available for fitting. Forecasts across several series in the same domain must use time spans and within = "domain", so that every series shares the cutoff. Count forecasts require one series per independent domain; within = "key" is rejected when it would leave another series' future observations available in that domain.

Usage

forecast_folds(
  data,
  initial = NULL,
  horizon,
  step = horizon,
  gap = NULL,
  window = c("expanding", "sliding"),
  lookback = NULL,
  origins = NULL,
  index = NULL,
  key = NULL,
  .by = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  within = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, tsibble, or cubble.

initial

Initial training span, measured from the first observation. Required unless origins is supplied.

horizon

Positive span assessed after each gap.

step

Positive distance between generated origins; defaults to horizon.

gap

Nonnegative span between training and assessment; defaults to zero in the same units and type as horizon.

window

"expanding" or "sliding" training window.

lookback

Positive training span for sliding windows. Training includes observations strictly after origin - lookback and through the origin.

origins

Optional explicit index values. Generated origins require a complete horizon within the observed range; explicit origins require at least one assessment and one training observation in each domain.

index, key, .by, id

Columns identifying time, series, independent domains, and unique observations. Use unquoted column names or tidy selections.

within

Choose "key" or "domain" for multiple series. Count spans require "key" and count rows in stable time order.

Value

A naboer_folds object. Generated empty assessment windows are skipped.
